172.t: The band splits and the Southern Yacht Club contract
172.s: Celestin and others tell the Southern Yacht Club he quit; Ridgley goes down, the club cancels them, and he plays with seven pieces.
172.q: Well, our band, we played at the Temple Roof Garden on a Wednesday night. Sillis Stain, the two Mareros and Paul Baum. They had a morning meeting. See? And the band, that's where they pulled out for me. Well, Lewis Madison, he was out among them and he heard of me. He called me up at 4 o'clock in…

172.t: Louis Cottrell Jr., Arthur Derbigny and Don Albert breaking up the band
172.s: Ridgley says Cottrell played with him briefly, and that Don Albert took Cottrell and Derbigny and broke up his band.
172.q: Let me see what time could that have been. He didn't stay too long. He was playing with me and another fellow came in. Let me see the name of my 20th player. He was playing with saxophone and Derby. He's dead. Arthur Derby is a violin player he was with me.

177.t: Celestin's wartime band and his later Dixieland turn
177.s: In 1941 Celestin, after a shipyard job and a broken leg, formed a band with Ricard Alexis, Albert Walters and others; Giles says Celestin was not originally a Dixieland man.
177.q: Yeah, they did, yeah, they played that way back. Really, he was a real great musician. And I played with Silly Stamp Band, made up a band, not our, he made the band up. This was in around, last of 41. He had, things had gotten bad and he had broke up his band. He didn't have any band, Silly Stamp,…

177.t: Papa Celestin's 1941 band and its members
177.s: Jiles played with Celestin for a few months in 1941 until Celestin was hurt, and names the sidemen.
177.q: Oh yeah, Celestan. I worked with him in 41 he made up a band. And at that time he had quit playing for a while, almost like give it up. And he started to make up a band. So I was playing with him and for then when the war come up you had to get a defense job. And he got a job now at the shipyard at…

662.t: Celestin's band during her absence, 1935 to 1953
662.s: She left in 1935 and rejoined in 1953. They discuss Celestin's wartime break, the Paddock period, Mercedes, and the musicians who stayed when she returned.
662.q: It wasn't at the time that I was with them. As I said, I stopped in 35 and then I didn't rejoin until 53. So it might have been during that period.

662.s: Russell asks about Celestin's two bands in the 1950s; she was away until she returned in 1953 and cannot say.
662.q: Well, I wasn't with them then, so I don't know anything about that. Well, didn't you come back? I came back in 53. Yes, but he had... He didn't have two bands then. He had them before.

55.t: Ridgley split and Celestin's 1949 Paddock comeback
55.s: The dollar dispute that split the Tuxedo bands and the comeback band that opened at the Paddock in 1949.
55.q: Not with me. Not on the records. Shots never didn't leave Ricard. Shots was stuck with Ricard. He stayed with Ricard. Shots and this boy, uh, but this boy, uh, played trombone. Well, they all stuck with Ricard. Yeah. David Jones and them, they stayed on the Pelican with Ricard. Emma Barris, all…

55.t: Celestin takes over the Paddock; his $300 demand
55.s: Celestin takes the job from Ridgley, falls ill, demands $300 a week from the Paddock owners, and Bill stays on with Ridgley.
55.q: And the next six months Celestine had taken the job over from Ricard. And that threw at Ricard and made everything go to Papa Celestine. You see? Everything was Papa Celestine. So Papa Celestine was sick then. I know he was very sick then. So he worked there a few years and got himself straightened…

307.t: Joining Celestin at the American Legion Hall; Paddock Lounge split
307.s: He started with Celestin at the American Legion Hall when Bill Matthews's group fell out with Papa, and later became regular clarinetist after Paul Barnes left.
307.q: Yes, in a way, I did because we started, I started with him at, let me see, it was at the American Legion Hall on Ross Street. Well, Bill Matthews and them were supposed to play there with him. And it seemed like they already stayed at the paddock lounge and played. It was a count of a day. So Papa…

307.t: Celestin's big band in 1946 and his comeback
307.s: Thomas wasn't in the 1946 big band at the Pelican; Celestin gave up music, worked at a shipyard, broke his leg, then made a comeback.
307.q: No, I wasn't. No, I wasn't with the band then. No, I heard about Shatz playing with the band. And, uh, I think there was one Papa had the big band. That was way back, I think. Yeah. They played at the Pelican. No, it was about 1946. They played with the big band.

282.t: Working with Celestin: dates, Bourbon Street and the band's end
282.s: He describes steady work in the city, a year at the Paddock on Bourbon Street, Celestin's death and Eddie Pearson taking over, and enjoying Celestin and Morgan best.
282.q: And after that, well, he said he were getting too old to fool around Bourbon Street. And he said, well, I'll pull the band out of Bourbon Street. And because I have enough work for you fellas to make a living without working on Bourbon Street. Mm-hmm. Well, a few years after that, Papa died.

286.t: Eddie Johnson reading band, Pete Lala's, and Kid Karkle
286.s: Eddie Johnson's band with Willie Foster managing; Russ quit and moved to the Pete Lala place band with Willie Karkle.
286.q: But it was Eddie Johnson's band. And Willie Foster was the manager. You see? It was a very Johnson job, but Willie Foster was the manager. You see? And it's a rehearsal, by Willie Foster's house.

306.t: Who took over after the 1942 break-up, and Papadie the drummer
306.s: Zander asks about Johnny Cicero; Rene says others took over after the trouble in 1942, and Russell identifies the drummer Papadie as surnamed Foster.
306.ch: Opening and the Budweiser Dance Hall
306.q: I think they must have took over because I know they left me after the scrummage. Yeah, yeah, yeah. In 42 that's the time they must have took over. Oh yeah this other little boy Papadie called him. He went back there. They had another section because after that scrummage happened I don't know.

270.t: Pensacola band breaks up and Sayles returns to join Bebe Ridgley's Pelican band
270.s: Eagle Eye hires Edmund Hall away, Albert Morgan goes home with Sam Morgan, Sayles returns to New Orleans c. 1927 and joins Ridgley's Pelican Roof band with David Jones directing.
270.ch: The Pelican band and Ridgley years
270.q: Well, I probably met him, a lot of the guys. He went to New York. Yeah. Well, that happened years later because now I want to get, you still get on that same kick in Jacksonville. Now, Eagle Eyes had came out somewhere and heard our band. In fact, we even went up and sat in with the band. And he…
